answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The registry records each stake at a vertex, while a harbor contract delays withdrawals until disputes expire; proven fraud burns part of the deposit. Creating a hundred identities then requires a hundred funded stakes, and attacking with them risks losing real capital, not merely generating names. A comet of short-lived accounts cannot evade that cost by appearing all at once.
